rules: Each entry carries a 'source' URL. A profile may only be shown in the UI when every TOPS value in it has a non-empty source.
These are PEAK CALCULATED values (Intel calls them PTOPS - Peak Tera Operations Per Second). The QRG footnote states they are calculated from assumptions, not measured.
The HUD must render them with the word 'peak' and the source URL available in the operator overlay.
Prefer runtime-reported numbers where available: read DEVICE_GOPS from OpenVINO (ov::device::gops / 'DEVICE_GOPS') in a try/except and display it next to the peak spec when present.
Fill/verify the entry for the demo machine's actual SKU from Intel ARK before the show.

profiles.family: Intel Core Ultra Series 2 (Lunar Lake, Core Ultra 200V)
profiles.source: Intel Core Ultra Series 2 (Lunar Lake) launch materials / platform brief - verify per-SKU on Intel ARK before the show
profiles.note: NPU TOPS = 48; Arc GPU = up to 67; platform total = up to 120.

profiles.source: Intel Core Ultra desktop (Series 2) product brief - NPU 13 TOPS; verify GPU/platform on Intel ARK per SKU
profiles.note: Same NPU silicon as Meteor Lake. Expect FEWER models to compile on the NPU than on Lunar Lake - the DeviceAvailability gate must handle that as a normal outcome, not an error.

profiles.source: Intel Core Ultra Series 3 Quick Reference Guide v1 (cdrdv2-public.intel.com/871380) - 'NEW NPU with up to 50 TOPS', up to 12 Xe cores; Intel CES 2026 Core Ultra Series 3 launch press deck - up to 180 TOPS platform
profiles.note: Per-SKU values differ (e.g. a Core 5 SKU in the launch deck shows up to 18 NPU TOPS / up to 2 Xe cores) - set the numbers for the exact SKU on the machine.
